headword: {苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したよう
reading: にがむしをかみつぶしたよう
gloss: looking sour; bitter-faced; looking extremely displeased

definitions.gloss: looking sour; bitter-faced; looking extremely displeased
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression describing a facial expression of extreme displeasure, irritation, or bitterness, as if one had bitten down on something intolerably bitter.

examples.japanese: {苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような{顔|かお}をしていた。
examples.english: He had a sour expression on his face.

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}は{報告|ほうこく}を{聞|き}いて、{苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような{表情|ひょうじょう}になった。
examples.english: Upon hearing the report, the department head's expression turned sour.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けた{監督|かんとく}は、{苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような{顔|かお}で{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: Having lost the match, the coach faced the press conference with a grimly bitter expression.

notes:
Literally "as if one had crushed a bitter bug in one's teeth." {苦虫|にがむし} is not a real insect — it is an imaginary creature used only in this idiom to evoke an intensely bitter taste. The expression vividly captures the tightened lips and furrowed brow of someone deeply displeased.

USAGE:
Almost always used in the pattern {苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような + noun (especially {顔|かお} or {表情|ひょうじょう}). Describes suppressed displeasure — the person is unhappy but not shouting or crying; instead, the emotion shows silently in their face.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような{顔|かお}: a bitter, sour face
- {苦虫|にがむし}を{噛|か}み{潰|つぶ}したような{表情|ひょうじょう}: a displeased expression

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {渋|しぶ}い{顔|かお}: a sour face; a reluctant look — less extreme; can imply reluctance rather than displeasure
- {不機嫌|ふきげん}な{顔|かお}: an ill-tempered face — more direct, less vivid
- {仏頂面|ぶっちょうづら}: a sulky face; scowl — implies stubbornness and refusal to engage
